depends_on.description: Resolved dependency relation between two releases.

registry_reports_signing_key.description: An ecosystem registry's metadata associates this artifact with this signing key. OBSERVATION ONLY: no cryptographic verification performed against artifact bytes. Policies requiring strong evidence MUST require `cryptographically_verified_signature_by`.

cryptographically_verified_signature_by.description: A signature over the artifact's bytes was fetched AND validated by this binary, in this run, against a known public key whose trust chain anchors to a pinned root (Fulcio public-good root for Sigstore). VERIFICATION class: occurrences naming this predicate MUST have attestor_role = verifier (epistemic-model.v1.md §3, invariant 16, layer-3.md §9). Federation imports may NEVER carry this predicate; at the boundary they are rewritten as peer_reports_* observation predicates.

cryptographic_verification_failed.description: This binary executed cryptographic verification of an attestation for the artifact and the verification did NOT succeed. The structured reason code (bundle_parse_failed, signature_invalid, certificate_chain_invalid, transparency_log_proof_invalid, subject_digest_mismatch, oidc_subject_coherence_failed, input_invalid, unknown) is recorded in the assertion's evidence sidecar (a sigstore.verification_failure raw record). REFUTATION class: positive evidence about our own verifier's behaviour, not a claim about the artifact (epistemic-model.v1.md §7.3). Occurrences naming this predicate MUST have attestor_role = verifier.

published_by.description: Identity recorded by the registry as publisher of a release.

published_at.description: Release timestamp as recorded by the registry.

affected_by.description: Artifact is affected by a vulnerability advisory.

attests_to.description: Attestation envelope refers to a subject.

revises.description: Supersession edge: this identity replaces another. Meta-predicate; carries no truth about the world, only about the log's organisation.

peer_reports_cryptographic_verification_.description: A federated peer claims to have cryptographically verified a signature for the artifact. The object is a ref to the foreign identity ID; the foreign verified-form identity is NOT stored locally (layer-3.5.md §1, invariant 16). OBSERVATION class: we did not verify anything ourselves. Promotion to local verified-form requires running the local verifier.

A federated peer claims their verifier rejected an attestation for the artifact. The object is a ref to the foreign identity ID. OBSERVATION class: the peer's negative judgement is our observation, not our refutation.

transparency_log_records_checkpoint.description: The local node submitted a checkpoint (a signed local-chain summary) to a transparency system and recorded the system's response. OBSERVATION class: the assertion records what was returned, not whether the timestamp is accurate, the provider is trustworthy, or the underlying log content is true. The evidence_id points at the bytes the provider returned. The subject is a checkpoint:<sha256> IRI naming a local checkpoint raw evidence record. Phase 5: tamper-evidence is strengthened by verify check #13, which cross-references the checkpoint's recorded (log_id, seq, chain_hash) triple against the current local chain. Inclusion-proof verification (a verification-class predicate) is deferred to Phase 5.5.

peer_reports_transparency_log_records_ch.description: A federated peer claims to have observed an anchor record for the named checkpoint. The object is a ref to the peer's foreign anchor identity ID. OBSERVATION class: this is our observation of the peer's observation; it inherits no authority from the original transparency system. Reserved in vocab v6 but typically NOT minted at the federation boundary — anchor identities are observation-class already and pass through unchanged. Implementations MAY mint this predicate if a policy author wants a structurally distinct per-source predicate; the canonical alternative is to join the occurrences table on attestor_role and log_id.
